Use this page when diabetes is part of your study: as an exposure, an
inclusion or exclusion criterion, or a covariate, and especially when you
need to tell type 1 from type 2 diabetes, which diagnosis codes in LPR (the
National Patient Register) alone do not do reliably. OSDC is an open source
algorithm, published as the R package `osdc`, that classifies diabetes from
diagnoses, prescriptions, podiatrist services and HbA1c results. You need
access to five registers (listed [below](#registers-osdc-needs)). You end with
one row per person with diabetes, their type and the date they enter the
diabetes population.

**Article:** [Isaksen et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.2147/CLEP.S407019), *Clinical Epidemiology*
**Documentation and code:**
[steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/)

The package README says that minor changes have been made to the algorithm
since the validated version in the article, and that more are expected; the
changes are listed in the repository.

## What OSDC gives you {#what-does-osdc-give-you}

`classify_diabetes()` returns one row per person classified as having
diabetes, with five columns. People without diabetes are not in the output:
"no diabetes" means "not in the table".

  | Column                      | Contents                                                             |
  | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `pnr`                       | Personal identifier                                                  |
  | `raw_inclusion_date`        | The date of the person's second inclusion event (inclusion requires two) |
  | `stable_inclusion_date`     | The same date, but `NA` if it falls before 1 January 1998            |
  | `has_t1d`                   | `TRUE`/`FALSE`: type 1 diabetes                                      |
  | `has_t2d`                   | `TRUE`/`FALSE`, defined as `!has_t1d`, so the two are complements    |

The inclusion events are HbA1c of 48 mmol/mol or more, a hospital diagnosis of
diabetes, a diabetes-specific podiatrist service and a purchase of
glucose-lowering drugs. The dates are inclusion dates, the date a person
enters the diabetes population, not a date of disease onset, and there is no
age at onset.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Choosing between the two dates is a study decision.** Before 1998 the
register data may not be good enough to tell new (incident) cases from
existing (prevalent) ones, so `stable_inclusion_date` is blank for inclusions
before then. The 1998 default is one year after pregnancy data in LPR became
usable for dropping purchases related to gestational diabetes. Filter on
`stable_inclusion_date` and every case included before 1998 leaves your
cohort without an error. Use `raw_inclusion_date` and you keep them, at the
cost of dates the package's authors flag as uncertain. Decide which, and say
which in your methods section. The cutoff is an argument,
`stable_inclusion_start_date`, if your LPR and LMDB data start later than
1997.
:::

## Run osdc on your project {#run-osdc}

`osdc` is on CRAN. Install it, then load it:

```r
install.packages("osdc")
library("osdc")
```

`install.packages()` installs dependencies that are missing, but it does not
update ones that are already installed; R's own help advises running
`update.packages()` first. The pre-installed packages on DST may be old, so if
`library("osdc")` stops with a version error, update the package it names.

`classify_diabetes()` takes one argument per register (`lpr`, `hsr`,
`lab_forsker`, `bef`, `lmdb`). Each must be a DuckDB table covering all the
years you have, for example a connection to your parquet files. LPR must
first be combined into one table, and so must the two health insurance
registers, with `join_registers()`. The getting-started guide,
[steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/articles/osdc.html](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/articles/osdc.html),
walks through this step by step.

::: {.callout-note}
**Is `osdc` available on your project?** It is confirmed on DARTER (project
708421). It is likely available on other projects too, but this has not been
verified. Check with `"osdc" %in% rownames(available.packages())` on your own
server (the package is not pre-installed, so `available.packages()` shows
whether it can be installed). If it is missing, you can ask DST to install it.
:::

## The registers osdc needs {#registers-osdc-needs}

`classify_diabetes()` uses BEF, LPR, LMDB, the health insurance registers
(`sysi`/`sssy`) and laboratory results, and needs all five: it has one
argument for each ([osdc design
vignette](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/articles/design.html)).

::: {.callout-warning}
**Missing one of the five?** Two different reasons, two different fixes:

- **`sysi`/`sssy`:** these are ordinary DST registers. If they are missing,
  your project has not requested them; ask for them to be added.
- **Laboratory results:** these are not a DST register. They come from the
  Danish Health Data Authority (Sundhedsdatastyrelsen) through a separate
  Forskerservice application, so they never appear in DST's own overview.
  See [Laboratory results](laboratory-results.qmd) for the table names and
  how the data are reached.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Which glucose-lowering drugs count as inclusion events?"}
Not every purchase of a glucose-lowering drug (ATC `A10`) counts:

- All GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 is glucagon-like peptide-1) are dropped,
  because this drug class is used extensively for weight loss in people
  without diabetes.
- Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin, two SGLT-2 inhibitors (sodium-glucose
  co-transporter 2), are dropped when bought on their own, because Danish
  guidelines recommend them for heart and kidney failure in people without
  diabetes.
- Combination drugs with a GLP-1 receptor agonist or an SGLT-2 inhibitor
  together with another glucose-lowering drug do count.
- Purchases during pregnancy are dropped, and so is metformin bought by women
  under 40 or with a polycystic ovary syndrome indication code.

The exact logic is in the [algorithm
vignette](https://steno-aarhus.github.io/osdc/articles/algorithm.html) and the
[code on GitHub](https://github.com/steno-aarhus/osdc).
:::

## The type is decided with data from after your index date {#type-uses-future-data}

::: {.callout-warning}
**Run on all years, the type classification uses information from after
your index date.** Type 1 versus type 2 is decided from the person's whole
record: the share of diagnoses that are type 1, and insulin purchase
patterns. A person's type can therefore depend on events that had not
happened on your index date. If you use the type as a baseline variable, you
classify people with information from the future (look-ahead
misclassification). This applies to a pre-computed population too, since it
is run on all years.

To avoid it, run `classify_diabetes()` yourself on register data filtered to
before your index date, so the classification only sees pre-index
information. If you change the algorithm itself, for example to count GLP-1
receptor agonists, the published validation no longer applies.
:::

## On DARTER: a pre-computed population {#darter-pre-computed}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="DARTER (project 708421): where the pre-computed files are, and the old population"}
On DARTER the OSDC classification is already computed, so you do not need to
run the algorithm yourself unless the look-ahead problem above matters for
your study. The path and the name `osdc` (and `read_register("osdc")`) are
DARTER-specific; on other projects the file is named differently and lives
elsewhere.

The 2024 population was generated, on the latest data, after the package was
updated and released on CRAN. It is valid for inclusions until the end of 2024 and replaces
the previous population file: use one or the other, never both. The previous
files are kept for reproducibility.

- **Parquet:** `E:/workdata/708421/cleaned-data/parquet-external/osdc/2024`,
  which `read_register("osdc")` finds on DARTER
- **`.csv`, `.rds` or `.dta`:**
  `E:/workdata/708421/cleaned-data/diabetes_register_pop/2024`

```r
library(fastreg) # read_register()
dm_pop <- read_register("osdc") # the 2024 population; DARTER only
```

**The previous population (up to 2022), for reproducibility only.** It has a
different output format; the column names below apply only to the old file.

```r
library(dplyr) # rename, filter, select

dm_pop <- readRDS("E:/workdata/708421/cleaned-data/diabetes-register-pop/dm_population_1977_2022.rds")

names(dm_pop)
# [1] "PNR"           "diabetes_type"  "do_dm"          "age_at_onset"

dm_pop <- dm_pop %>% rename(pnr = PNR) # lower-case pnr, as everywhere else

# diabetes_type: 1 = T1D, 2 = T2D  |  do_dm: the date in the old file

t1d <- dm_pop %>%
  filter(diabetes_type == 1) %>% # type 1 only
  select(pnr, diabetes_type, do_dm) %>%
  rename(date_diabetes = do_dm)
```
:::
